steps.content: <size=42><color=#7683a2>[DISMYTH] [Chat Room]</color> [Spoilers] [About "The Burning Redwood"...] [Comments: 400+]</size>

<color=#fb9259>Outsider_ [OP]</color>: I've been getting a lot of requests in my DMs lately, so I'll make a dedicated post to explain.

<color=#fb9259>Outsider_ [OP]</color>: The legend of "The Burning Redwood" dates back over a decade. Supposedly, a cursed street in Eastside was about to be torn down and rebuilt when a mysterious fire suddenly engulfed it.

<color=#fb9259>Outsider_ [OP]</color>: The blaze raged for three days and three nights. Nothing could put it out... The flames lit up half of Eastside, like <color=#ff0000>a massive burning redwood</color>.

<color=#fb9259>Outsider_ [OP]</color>: Ever since, rumors have been all over the place. What's true and what's not? Honestly, I'm not even sure the place ever existed.

<color=#7683a2>Da3m0n</color>: I knew it!!! I knew there was more to this than meets the eye! Another case, how exciting!

<color=#7683a2>Sphinx_0527</color>: Ugh... who even digs up some cold case like this to write about? Clout-chasing much? Plus, didn't this case barely get any attention to begin with?

<color=#7683a2>Crimson_Storm</color>: Wait... remember that rumor about Clementine? How disaster always follows after she publishes a book... Do you think there's a chance...

<color=#7683a2>Crimson_Storm</color>: That the incident is connected to this fire?
#Renowned Author Clementine Unearths Old Cold Case?# #Does The Burning Redwood in Murder on the Praeva Express Really Exist?# #Bestselling Novel Leads to Bizarre Fire? Just What Might the Truth Be?#
Speculation begins to spiral. Searches for "The Burning Redwood" skyrocket, and related topics climb the trending lists. All questions, all theories, ultimately converge on a single question—
[Scene Transition - Clementine's Study]

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: What connection does your book have with the fire from N.F. 105?

The study remains as warm and cozy as before. Clementine still sits across from you. She rises to refill your tea, her smile veiled behind the rising steam, making her expression impossible to read. For some inexplicable reason, it sends a chill down your spine.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: A victim appears, the mystery explodes... The story is on the right track, and the buzz has reached its peak.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Chief, my little marketing trick worked rather well, wouldn't you agree?

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: ...You emphasized that your story is set in a fictional, retro world before Nightfall. Yet, you deliberately left breadcrumbs for people to follow, leading them to dig deeper into whether the incident behind it was real or fabricated. I'll admit, as a marketing strategy, it was remarkably effective.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: That is, assuming this book really is, as you claim, <color=#fb9259>completely fictional</color>.
You did consider the possibility that the crime foretold in "Praeva" might have already occurred, but... a fire from decades ago?
You meet Clementine's gaze directly, trying to find some kind of opening in her composure.

options: I'm sure you've got better things to do as well. How about you come clean already?

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: Is The Burning Redwood real or not? And what connection does The Praeva Express have with that fire?

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: Just which parts of your story are <color=#fb9259>fictional</color>, and which parts are <color=#fb9259>real</color>?

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Believe me, Chief, I'd love to cooperate. Unfortunately, though, I'm obligated to stay silent.
Clementine taps her chin lightly, almost like she's genuinely troubled by such an absurd predicament.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: The thing is, I've signed an extremely strict contract with my publisher. If I reveal even a single word more than I should before "Praeva" is fully released, I'll have lawyers knocking at my door and demanding compensation by tomorrow.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: The conclusion to the mystery is what makes my novel valuable. If the truth were revealed prematurely, the book wouldn't be able to sell.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: However...
Her fingers conceal the grin she's wearing. The woman before you is just like some ancient fox spirit from folklore—she's cunning incarnate.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: If the "detective" can deduce the answer themself using the clues in the book, that wouldn't count as me giving spoilers, would it?

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: Has anyone ever told you that your acting is terrible?

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Oh my, was it that bad?
The contract is just an excuse. You can tell. She's making things difficult on purpose.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: You'd really go through all this trouble just to make me keep reading your book?

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Writing is no easy task. Naturally, a writer would like to preserve their story's secrets until readers reach the ending.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: It wouldn't hurt to indulge in this little game now, would it? Think of it as a <color=#fb9259>deduction challenge</color>.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: As both reader and detective, you must search the book for clues that are hidden in the smallest details, just like anyone else. And then, you'll ultimately uncover the mastermind behind these heinous crimes...

options: What makes you so sure I'll play along?

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: My MBCC team is right outside this building. I wouldn't mind continuing this conversation elsewhere, you know.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: True. But if you really wanted to use force, you could've dragged me back to the MBCC the moment you walked in.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: You didn't haul me in for questioning... That makes me think we're on the same page—we both want to keep this little misunderstanding between us.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Authors hate spoilers, but I'm more than happy to guide you on your journey to the truth.
The book's pages open before you once more. The illustration of the victim is strikingly disturbing.
The bloodstains beside the victim spread out like butterfly wings. You look up and see the wall of butterfly specimens behind Clementine. They seem to mirror the deaths written in her book.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Rest assured, Chief. I promise... whatever it is that you're looking for, you'll find the clues you need in this book.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: So... read it, and solve the mystery—
[Black Screen, Small Avatar Mode]

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: <color=#fb9259>Just who on this train killed "Clementine"?</color>
